title: acp/1 report
description: Describes the dict actually returned/persisted by FileTransport.report() / Conversation.report() in agent-comms/src/acp (there is no Pydantic model for Report yet; it is built as a plain dict). This diverges substantially from the Report record in docs/agent-communication-protocol.md's 'Core model and envelope' table (`from`, `status`, `stage`, `output_ref`, `checks[]`, `summary`); see docs/decisions.md (2026-09-29) for the full comparison. It also diverges from the *separate*, non-acp/1 report shape that the legacy handoff_compat.py shim persists to $FACTORY_DIR/reports/ (which is a much closer match to the doc, having been modeled on the workshop's own `handoff report`, predating this file). This schema covers only the acp/1 core-library shape.

from.description: The doc calls this field `from`, consistent with the Envelope's sender field naming.

message_id.description: The message this report answers. Not in the doc's Report record at all: the doc's report is keyed by convention (current attempt + role), not tied to a specific message_id. Doc has no equivalent field.

outcome.description: The doc calls this field `status` and gives it a much richer, domain-flavoured vocabulary (e.g. implemented, review-pass, review-fail, blocked-access, needs-human, failed, acknowledged -- the same terminal statuses the legacy handoff report and handoff_compat.py use). The acp/1 core library instead hard-codes a generic pass/fail/blocked outcome (see cli.py's `--outcome` choices).

checks.description: A map of check-name -> exit code (e.g. {"pytest": 0}). The doc specifies `checks[]`: an array. This schema follows the real implementation (an object), not the doc.

verified.description: True when every value in `checks` is 0 (and, notably, also True when `checks` is empty -- an empty check list is 'verified' by this implementation's `all(...)` logic). Not named or described anywhere in the doc; closest in spirit to the doc's implicit 'checks_passed'.
